newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Gehe boosted by Lloyds, pound rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gehe boosted by Lloyds, pound rise.

text.p: German drug wholesaler Gehe AG on Wednesday declared the integration of its new British subsidiary Lloyds Chemists a success and said the unit boosted its sales and profits in the first half of 1997.

Gehe clinched the deal for Lloyds Chemists in January after a year-long takeover battle with Unichem Plc. The Stuttgart-based firm out-gunned Unichem with a cash bid of 685 million pounds, securing itself a strong role in British retail pharmacy.
Gehe said in a statement that its pre-tax profit rose 15.4 percent to 226.5 million marks ($121.4 million) in the first six months of 1997, with Lloyds Chemists making a "positive" contribution.
Sales rose 18.3 percent to 12.4 billion marks, but the advance would have been just four percent discounting Lloyds and a separate drugs unit sell-off.
Gehe said it had made 230 million pounds by selling off non-core operations at Lloyds Chemists, in line with the takeover conditions set by the British government.

The company also said it had gained more than 400 million marks in "hidden reserves" on its recently-acquired British subsidiaries, whose mark values have soared on the back of the pound's ascent against the German currency.

Chief financial officer Karl Eick said in a telephone interview the company would have to pay 180 million marks more today for Lloyds and 250 million marks more for British group AAH, the drugs wholesaler Gehe bought in 1995 in a deal valued at around 400 million pounds.

The pound has soared this year, gaining around 19 percent against the mark at its most recent highest point. At Wednesday's levels the pound was showing an 11 percent gain versus the mark over the year.

Gehe predicted full-year profits would increase by 15 to 20 percent and repeated an earlier forecast that sales, including Lloyds, would hit 24.5 billion marks by the end of the year, up from 21.4 billion in 1996.
Lloyds had already been "smoothly" integrated with Gehe's own British unit AAH, Gehe said.
AAH's 322 pharmacies have linked up with Lloyds' 904 outlets to create a new British retail pharmacy division.

Gehe said it had set up a new management team to oversee the newly-merged AAH/Lloyds pharmaceutical wholesale business in Britain and had decided to establish a joint administrative centre in Coventry.
